newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures drift to mixed close.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures drift to mixed close.

text.p: IMM currency futures drifted to a mixed close after another session in which most units languished inside familiar territory.
Late activity focused mainly on Sterling, where traders said one firm was seen buying about 1,000 December futures between 1.5730-34.
They figured the futures buying was intended as a hedge for an options position held by a large Mideast speculator.
Otherwise, afternoon activity stayed quiet, especially after the early close in U.S. Treasury bond futures ahead of Monday's partial U.S. holiday for Columbus Day.
IMM currency futures on Monday, October 14, will close two hours early at 1200 CDT/1700 GMT.
Traders said Friday's spate of U.S. economic data, which suggested inflation remained under control, did little to alter fundamental bullishness for the U.S. dollar.
"Last week shook some people when we opened the Swiss (franc) 40 points higher...(but) I think most people are still friendly the dollar," said one floor broker.
"We had three impressive moves today," said another floo r broker. "We closed above 1.53 dollar/mark. That's positive. We're closed above 111.50 dollar/yen. That's real positive."
"And the Canadian dollar hit major support and bounce right off it," the broker added of the $0.7395 level for December Canadian dollar futures.
He noted that sentiment also still leaned toward the upside for the Canadian unit technically, even though it had punched below a triple bottom at $0.7405.
"We blew right through it fast and hard...and came back up through it just as fast," he added.
Canadian dollar fell after joblessness there last month rose more than expected. Unemployment rose to 9.9 percent from 9.4 percent in August and versus forecasts for no change.
But the unit partly recovered technically and when no Canadian rate cut materialized during the Chicago session.
Currencies moved little after September U.S. producer prices rose 0.2 percent and gained 0.3 percent in the core rate, near forecasts.
September retail sales jumped 0.7 percent and rose 0.4 percent without autos. But that was offset by big downward revisions to August's figures.
December Sterling hit a new contract high at 1.5760 after unifying speeches by U.K. prime minister John Major and chancellor Kenneth Clarke.

December yen ended down $0.000036 at $0.009039, marks eased $0.0011 to $0.6559, Swiss francs fell $0.0027 to $0.8030, Sterling jumped $0.0096 to $1.5748, Canadian dollar ended flat at $0.7427, Aussie dollar rose $0.0006 to $0.7887, and Mexican peso skidded $0.000800 to $0.125700. -Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
